question: Should OpenClaw adopt a built-in prompt-bearing Markdown policy, and which workspace, skill-read, install, and publishing surfaces should block, warn, quarantine, tag, or defer to operator policy?
rationale: Pattern selection, false-positive tolerance, trust-boundary ownership, compatibility behavior, and whether findings may stop existing prompts or installs are security and product choices that source inspection cannot safely determine.

options.title: Shared layered policy
options.body: Create a common finding taxonomy, warn or quarantine by default, expose findings through ClawHub and local diagnostics, and allow blocking through high-confidence rules or `security.installPolicy`.

options.title: Strict built-in enforcement
options.body: Fail closed on a maintainer-approved rule set across prompt ingestion and skill installation, accepting compatibility and false-positive risk.

options.title: Keep enforcement external
options.body: Leave blocking to ClawHub and `security.installPolicy`, document local prompt files as trusted state, and avoid a core runtime content scanner.

recommendation.title: Shared layered policy
recommendation.body: Create a common finding taxonomy, warn or quarantine by default, expose findings through ClawHub and local diagnostics, and allow blocking through high-confidence rules or `security.installPolicy`.
